[[Prince]] '''Andrey Petrovich Gagarin''' (Russian: Андрей Петрович Гагарин; 9 July 1934 – 30 January 2011) was a professor of physics at [[Saint Petersburg Polytechnical University]].

==Ancestry and background==

As the son of Prince [[Peter Andreevich Gagarin]] (Russian: Князь Петр Андреевич Гагарин, 1904–1938) and grandson of Prince Andrey Grigorievich Gagarin (Russian: Князь Андрей Григорьевич Гагарин, 1855–1920), Andrey Petrovich Gagarin walked in the footsteps of his closest ancestors. His father was a graduate of the same Polytechnical University for which his grandfather was the first rector,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spbstu-eng.ru/index.php5?module=articles&class=showArticles&configId=1&tpl=single&articleId=1&MenuId=abaabaaba |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120918105258/http://www.spbstu-eng.ru/index.php5?module=articles&class=showArticles&configId=1&tpl=single&articleId=1&MenuId=abaabaaba |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-09-18 |title=Origins |publisher=Spbstu-eng.ru |date=1902-10-02 |accessdate=2012-01-20 }}</ref> and at which Andrey Petrovich Gagarin held a professorship. His Great-grandfather was the diplomat, artist, officer and the vice-chancellor of the [[Imperial Academy of Arts]] Prince [[Grigory Gagarin|Grigory Grigorievich Gagarin]] (Russian: Князь Григорий Григорьевич Гагарин, 1810–1893), himself a son of Prince Grigory Ivanovich Gagarin (Russian: Князь Григорий Иванович Гагарин, 1782–1837), poet, diplomat and patron of the arts, later an ambassador to Rome.<ref name="rurik.genealogia.ru">{{Cite web|url=http://rurik.genealogia.ru/Rospisi/Gagarin3.htm|title = Князья Гагарины (третья ветвь). Родословная роспись}}</ref>

After the Bolshevik seizure of power, most members of the Gagarin family left the country. Still some decided to stay, a decision that proved dire. In 1938 Andrey would become the last Gagarin heir on Russian soil, after his father Peter Andreevich was executed during one of Stalin's purges.<ref>{{cite web |title=Список граждан, расстрелянных в Ленинграде, вне Ленинграда и впоследствии реабилитированных (том 8 "ЛМ") |url=http://visz.nlr.ru/search/lists/t8/227_0.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110617132821/http://visz.nlr.ru/search/lists/t8/227_0.html |archive-date=2011-06-17 |publisher=Visz.nlr.ru |accessdate=2012-01-20}}</ref> His older brother Andrey Andreevich had been executed the year prior. This left young Andrey Petrovich Gagarin, at the age of 4, one of the very few surviving [[Rurik dynasty#Legacy|Rurikid princes]] in Russia. He was raised by his mother Princess Varvara Vasilievna Gagarina (née Sheshina, later remarried to Vadim Mikhailovich Burlakov).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://baza.vgdru.com/1/37616/|title = ШЕШИН :: Персональный список}}</ref> By using the surname of his stepfather (during 1947–1972),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://baza.vgdru.com/1/4829/|title = БУРЛАКОВ :: Персональный список}}</ref> Andrey was able to obtain a higher education that would otherwise not have been accessible in Soviet Russia for a member of the former aristocracy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sta-net.ru/memory/263.html |title=Лучшая половина жизни |publisher=Sta-net.ru |accessdate=2012-01-20 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309051307/http://www.sta-net.ru/memory/263.html |archivedate=2012-03-09 }}</ref>

Prince Andrey P. Gagarin served as the chairman of the Nobility assembly of St. Petersburg<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spbgds.ru/ |title=Санкт-Петербургское губернское Дворянское собрание |publisher=Spbgds.ru |date= |accessdate=2012-01-20}}</ref> and was a long-time [[CILANE]] delegate.

==Marriages and Issue==

Andrey Petrovich Gagarin had married three times. His first marriage was to Tatiana Andreevna Shmit, no issue. His second marriage was to Tatiana Valentinovna Jakovleva and had issue:

* Princess Maria Andreevna Gagarina.

His final marriage was to Tatiana Ivanovna Nukhina and had issue:

* Prince Dmitri Andreevich Gagarin (born 1973). Legitimated by parents marriage.<ref name="civil.consultant.ru">{{cite web|url=http://civil.consultant.ru/reprint/books/211/16.html |title=Ахакхнрейю Пеопхмрмшу Хгдюмхи \ Йнмяскэрюмрокчя: Йкюяяхйю Пняяхияйнцн Опюбю |publisher=Civil.consultant.ru |date= |accessdate=2012-01-20}}</ref>
* Princess Julia Andreevna Gagarina. Legitimitated by parents marriage.<ref name="civil.consultant.ru"/> Julia Gagarina is married to Jan Alexander von Heiroth.

==Title and dynastic branch==

The title [[Knyaz]] (князь) is a Slavic title found in most Slavic languages, denoting a royal or a noble rank. It is usually translated into English as either Prince or less commonly as Duke. In Russia the title was originally a hereditary title for the patrilineal descendants of Rurik.<ref>"князь". "Vasmer's Etymological Dictionary" online</ref><ref>"knez". Oxford English Dictionary, 1989, online [1] (subscription required)</ref>  The [[Gagarin family|princes Gagarin]] are a cadet line of the [[House of Rurik]], descending from the Monomakh branch of the Rurikids.<ref>{{cite web
 |author     = Manaev, G.
 |url        = https://www.rbth.com/history/330627-rurik-dynasty-founded-russia-ruled-before-romanovs
 |title      = Who founded Russia and ruled it before the Romanovs?
 |publisher  = Russia Beyond the Headlines
 |date       = 2019-07-08
 |accessdate = 2020-01-29
}}</ref>
